name: Mysuru–Kushalnagar Highway
history: This is the road west from Mysuru towards Kodagu, the coffee-growing hill district also known as Coorg. It is being upgraded into a four-lane, part access-controlled highway to carry the heavy tourist traffic that pours into the hills every weekend and to speed up the movement of coffee, pepper and timber down to Mysuru.
facts: The main road from Mysuru into Kodagu, India's best-known coffee district.
Part of NH 275, which runs from Bengaluru through Mysuru to Mangaluru.
It passes Srirangapatna, the island fortress capital of Tipu Sultan.
Weekend tourist traffic from Bengaluru and Mysuru to Madikeri travels this way.
significance: Kodagu's coffee estates and hill resorts depend on this road for both their crop and their visitors, and it is the western continuation of the Bengaluru–Mysuru expressway corridor.

travelNotes: Busiest on Friday evenings and Sunday afternoons with weekend traffic to Coorg. Sections are under widening, so expect diversions.
